newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's annual mine wage talks to start Friday.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's annual mine wage talks to start Friday.

text.p: South Africa's mining industry and the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) will start annual wage increase negotiations on Friday, the Chamber of Mines employer body said on Wednesday.
"That's correct. The talks will start on Friday," said Chamber spokesman Llewellyn Kriel.
The Chamber represents and negotiates on behalf of coal and gold mine management. Wage talks are held every year.
Kriel declined to give the industry's opening offer.
"It is not our policy to negotiate through the media. Should our offer be known it will have come from sources other than ourselves," he said.
The NUM, representing about 350,000 mineworkers, is seeking a 20 percent wage increase and a minimum wage of 1,500 rand a month for surface workers and 1,800 rand for underground workers.
Gold and coal wage talks will take place separately to accommodate differing levels of profitability in the mining of the two minerals, Kriel said.
This year's wage talks are likely to be clouded by the threat of job cuts and shaft closures at a number of gold mines.

South Africa's gold mining industry has been hard hit by a weak bullion price and announced disappointing March quarter results with many mines saying that return to profitability could only be achieved through cutting costs further.

Mining house JCI Ltd announced last month it planned to retrench a third of its workforce at its Randfontein Estates Gold Mining Co Ltd. On Monday it said it would postpone the job cuts until the end of this week.

Presenting its first quarter gold results in April, Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd also warned of shaft closures and job cuts at its Free State Consolidated Gold Mine Ltd and Vaal Reefs Exploration and Mining Co Ltd .

Last year a wage deal was clinched three months after negotiations began. Most miners won wage increases of eight to 10 percent. South Africa's April consumer price inflation was 9.9 percent compared to March's 9.6 percent.
